classification.difficultyReason: Find the remaining central angle before applying the angle-at-the-centre theorem.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: An inscribed triangle with radii from O to all three vertices. The full angle w at the lower-left vertex includes the radius through that angle.
spec.mathematics: The central sectors between the top and lower-left radii and between the lower-left and lower-right radii are 120 degrees and 100 degrees. The remaining central sector subtends the same arc as w.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 120°, 100°, O and w are visible in the question diagram; the supplied 70° answer is omitted.

answer.worked:
The remaining angle at the centre is
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta &= 360^\circ-120^\circ-100^\circ\\
\theta &= 140^\circ.
\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{aligned}
w &= \frac{140^\circ}{2}\\
w &= 70^\circ.
\end{aligned}$$
